svg.text: LLM Quantization: Running 70B Models on a Laptop
From FP32 to INT4: how reducing precision cuts memory 8x with minimal quality loss
Each format uses different bit widths to represent the same number. Fewer bits = less memory but less precision.
A 7B model needs 28GB in FP32 but only 3.5GB in INT4 -- the difference between needing a datacenter and running on a laptop.
RTX 4090 (24GB) can run: 7B INT4, 13B INT4 | MacBook Pro M3 Max (64GB) can run: 70B INT4
Different methods trade off speed, quality, and hardware compatibility.
Used by: Ollama, LM Studio, local

As explained in our KV-cache deep dive, the cache grows with context length. Quantizing it provides additional memory savings.
Fits on single A100 40GB with room for activations!
Key: INT4 is the sweet spot for local deployment (8x smaller, ~5% quality loss) | INT8 for production serving | FP16 when quality is critical | GGUF for CPU/mixed, AWQ/GPTQ for GPU-only
